verdicts.label: A
verdicts.evidence: For the complete graph K_n, f(G) = n(n-1)(n-2)/6 and g(G) = n(n-1)(n-2)(n-3)/24. The ratio g(G)^3/f(G)^4 = (3/32) * (n-3)^3 / (n(n-1)(n-2)), which approaches 3/32 as n goes to infinity. According to the Kruskal-Katona theorem for cliques, the maximum value of g(G) for a given f(G) is achieved by a graph that is as close to a complete graph as possible, meaning the maximum value of the ratio is 3/32.

verdicts.label: B
verdicts.evidence: The ratio g(G)^3/f(G)^4 is bounded by 3/32, and 81/32 is significantly larger than this bound. No known graph exceeds the 3/32 limit.

verdicts.label: C
verdicts.evidence: For the complete graph K_5, f(G) = 10 and g(G) = 5, so g(G)^3/f(G)^4 = 125/10000 = 1/80. Since 1/80 > 1/256, the constant c = 1/256 is not an upper bound for all graphs.
